chunk_findings.detail: The module docstring states a write is inert when `.ddflow/local/config.toml` **or an environment variable** sets the same key, but only the `"local"` source is recognised. For any non-local winner, `who = _WINNER.get(source, f"the {source} setting")` degrades to a generic "the <source> setting" (it does not name the layer or, for env, the variable), and `fix` becomes the non-command `"unset it there"`. So with an env override, e.g. `schedule.max_parallel_tasks` exported in the environment and then `ddflow config schedule.max_parallel_tasks 7`, the user is warned the write is shadowed but is given neither the identity of the winning layer nor a usable command, which is exactly what the change's stated goal requires ("say the command that sets the winning layer"). The env case is the only actionable path a user has, and it is the one left as a stub.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/config_shadow.py:14 (`_WINNER` / `fix` in `shadow_report`)

chunk_findings.detail: `shadowed` is derived purely from layer precedence (`source not in (layer, "default")`); the note then unconditionally asserts `"{value!r}, not what was just written."` When the higher layer already holds the same value as the write, that sentence is false. Input: `.ddflow/local/config.toml` already contains `schedule.max_parallel_tasks = 7`, then `ddflow config schedule.max_parallel_tasks 7` without `--local` prints "the effective value of schedule.max_parallel_tasks is 7, not what was just written" — 7 *is* what was just written. The warning is still warranted (the committed file is inert), but the comparison text is wrong and will confuse the user about whether the value differs.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test bakes in the exact behaviour the bug report calls harmful, and in doing so contradicts the stated fix. The stated fix is: "for keys marked machine-local (parallelism, endpoints, reviewers) default to the local layer or ask" — and `KEY = "schedule.max_parallel_tasks"` is precisely a parallelism key, i.e. machine-local. The test nevertheless runs `run_cli(repo, "config", KEY, "7")` with no `--local` and then asserts `(repo / ".ddflow" / "config.toml").read_text("utf-8").count("max_parallel_tasks = 7")`, i.e. it requires that the machine-local value 7 *does* land in the committed project layer — the very thing the reporter had to `git checkout` away. Worse, the test can only pass if that default-to-committed path is taken: had the implementation applied the documented "default [machine-local keys] to the local layer", the second write would go to `.ddflow/local/config.toml` (overwriting the 6 set on the previous line), no layer would shadow it, and the test would fail on both `assert "7" in text and "shadow" in text` (line 18) and the final `read_text(...).count(...)` assertion. The `--json` variant has the same coupling (`body["effective"] == 6` / `body["shadowed"] is True`). So the change ships a regression test that asserts the shadowing-and-committing scenario must remain possible for parallelism keys, and it will reject any implementation that actually does what the intent describes; the test should instead assert that the machine-local key is routed to (or prompts for) the local layer, or at minimum that the committed file is left untouched.
